summary: Intro discovery for Kythera Consulting evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Primary concerns: model choice for multilingual customer support (EN/ES/JP), context window for long conversation history (~50k tokens per session), tool calling to internal CRM & doc retriever, latency targets for real-time chat (<=200ms token latency), and data residency/VPC needs. Agreed next steps: send perf spreadsheet, security docs, schedule SE deep-dive and run pilot benchmarks with provided prompt set.
topics: Open model tradeoffs (LLM families and quantization)
Context length and KV cache behavior
Deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
Security / compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off—this is Sophie from Redwood, with Devon and Ravi from our SE team. Michael, Aisha, Tom, Lina, thanks for making time. Quick agenda: understand your workloads, context sizes, multilingual needs, and how you want to call tools.

[00:18] Michael (Kythera CTO): Yeah thanks, Sophie. To be clear we're looking at multiple deployment options — ideally hosted to move fast but we might need dedicated or private for some customers. Main driver is conversational support for enterprise clients in NA, LATAM, and JP.

[00:35] Sophie: Got it. Maybe start with current infra — where are you running things now?

[00:40] Aisha (Lead ML Eng): Right now most of our infra is on GCP, with some customers in Azure. We use a mix of open models, a couple custom fine-tunes, and a retrieval stack with Pinecone for vectors. We've looked at running inference ourselves with Triton but it's brittle and ops heavy.

[00:59] Devon (Redwood SE): When you say "mix of open models"—which families? Llama-like, Mistral, Meta Llama-3, Llama-4?

[01:05] Aisha: Mostly Mistral-like families and Llama v3 variants; we've experimented with Mistral-7b and a quantized Llama-3. The problem is tradeoffs: Mistral seems strong on multilingual but context length is limited unless we do expensive sharding/kv work.

[01:22] Ravi (Redwood SE): Right, our runtime handles KV cache and prefix caching to avoid re-tokenizing. Curious—how long is a typical session history you want to keep accessible?

[01:29] Aisha: For some enterprise accounts we need 30k–60k tokens of convo history plus retrieved docs. The support agents want prior conversation, policy docs, and some PDFs in the prompt so effective context needs are big.

[01:45] Tom (SRE): Latency is also a thing for chat. We currently aim for sub-200ms per-token for agent-facing chat. For customer-facing (async) we can tolerate higher.

[01:54] Sophie: Helpful. So primary constraints: long context, multilingual (EN/ES/JP), tool-calling to CRM and our internal ticketing, and low token latency for agents. Do you have quality thresholds — e.g., acceptable fallbacks if a large-context model costs too much?

[02:10] Michael: We'd accept a hybrid: use a long-context model for agent sessions, and a cheaper short-context variant for simple bot replies. Cost targets are roughly 40% below current self-hosted ops if possible.

[02:22] Devon: Understood. A couple of notes on models: open families vary — some handle multilingual better out of the box (Mistral + fine-tunes), others scale in context (certain Llama-4 variants with 200k windows), and quantization can reduce cost but sometimes harms generation quality in Japanese.

[02:39] Aisha: That's been our experience — quantizing hurts non-English generation unless you tune carefully.

[02:45] Ravi: We typically recommend a split: a 100k-window model for agent context (when needed) and a 32k or 64k cheaper model for general user bot traffic. Redwood Dedicated lets you lock hardware and get predictable throughput; Private gives you VPC + KMS, and Hosted is fastest to go live.

[03:03] Aisha: Important question — tool-calling. We need function-like calls: retrieve a customer record, open a ticket, call our internal knowledge graph. Can Redwood do that and also maintain audited logs for each tool invocation?

[03:15] Devon: Yes — our tool-calling supports structured tool APIs; we can emit a structured JSON call and then you run a secure connector. We also surface invocation logs in the Console; audit trails are retained per your retention policy and we can route logs to your SIEM in Private deployments. Sometimes the transcription spelled "tool calling" as two words, but yes.

[03:32] Lina (Product): Is it easy to trigger different models or rollbacks based on LL confidence or latency? We want graceful fallback to a cheaper model when load spikes.

[03:39] Ravi: Absolutely — our smart routing can A/B or fallback by policy. You can route by latency SLO or cost threshold, and we support automatic fallback to a pinned variant. Rollouts are canary by default.

[03:50] Michael: On security — SOC2 compliance is a must for enterprise customers. Also we need SAML SSO for admin console, RBAC, and customer data residency for EU customers.

[03:59] Sophie: We have SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO integrations, fine-grained RBAC, and KMS/HSM support for Private. We'll attach the security pack. For hosted customers we offer data encryption at rest and access controls; if you need data residency we can route to region-specific deployments.

[04:17] Tom: Egress constraints — some customers won't allow outbound internet from the VPC. Can Private handle isolated on-prem or VPC with no egress?

[04:24] Ravi: Yes — Private deployments can be air-gapped or with strict egress rules. We offer an on-prem bundle and can do VPC peering with limited egress; connectors run inside your network. We'll need to validate the network diagram though.

[04:36] Aisha: About benchmarking — we want to run a pilot with our prompt set across 3 model candidates: Mistral-Enhanced-100k, LlamaX-100k-window (quantized), and Redwood-verified 32k variant. We'll measure token latency, hallucination rate on our eval set, and multilingual BLEU-ish metrics.

[04:53] Devon: Perfect. If you share the prompt set and representative docs, we can spin up a benchmark in Dedicated or Hosted (dev environment) and provide token-level traces and per-route cost breakdowns. Note that quantized LlamaX often has lower latency but sometimes higher hallucination in JP — we'll flag that in the results.

[05:10] Michael: Do you have any out-of-the-box connectors for popular CRMs? Salesforce, Zendesk?

[05:16] Sophie: We have native integrations for Salesforce and support for vector DB connectors (Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus). For custom systems we provide a secure connector template and webhooks.

[05:26] Lina: Pricing question — how do we estimate cost for a pilot? We need delta vs self-hosting and a rough monthly for 5 agent seats with heavy usage.

[05:33] Sophie: We'll provide a pilot estimate — typical pilots use Dedicated reserved slots for consistent latency. We'll send a detailed cost model: tokens, throughput, reserved capacity, and expected savings from intelligent batching + prefix caching. That's part of the spreadsheet Devon will share.

[05:47] Tom: Network latency — if we deploy Private in our AWS region (ap-northeast-1 for JP), does Redwood support region placement?

[05:54] Ravi: Yes, Private and Dedicated can be placed in your chosen region, and Hosted has region options. We'll note AP-Northeast for the pilot.

[06:02] Aisha: QA — during the pilot, can we capture per-token logits or other debug traces for model introspection? We need to reproduce odd hallucinations.

[06:10] Devon: We can provide trace hooks and token probability traces in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have more limited traces but we can surface generation metadata. We'll document what level of debug is available per deployment mode.

[06:22] Michael: One more — multilingual fallback: if a user writes in Spanish but model is weaker, do you recommend automatic translation + English model vs native Spanish model?

[06:29] Ravi: It depends. For high-fidelity ops we'd prefer native multilingual models; for cost-sensitive flows, translate to English and back can be ok but adds latency and risk of meaning loss. We can set routing policies so high-priority sessions go to native models.

[06:44] Sophie: Logistics — timeline? How fast can you do a pilot?

[06:48] Aisha: We could be ready to run tests in 1–2 weeks if we get access to a test environment and Redwood provides the benchmark harness.

[06:54] Sophie: Great — we'll target next Tuesday for the SE deep-dive. Action items recap: Devon sends perf spreadsheet, Sophie sends security pack and Private checklist, Aisha shares prompt sets, Tom confirms network constraints. We'll also float a 4-week pilot with success metrics: token latency under 200ms for agent flows 95% of the time, hallucination under X (we'll define), and multilingual correctness improvement over current baseline.

[07:18] Michael: Sounds good. Quick note — we might bring procurement in if the pilot looks promising, so please include rough T&Cs and pilot pricing band.

[07:28] Sophie: Will do. I'll include a one-page pilot agreement template and pricing bands.

[07:34] Lina: Also please share any references of customers in JP or LATAM using long-context variants — would help with buy-in.

[07:40] Ravi: We'll include anonymized references and a couple of case notes.

[07:46] (brief crosstalk)

[07:50] Michael: Thanks all — that covered it.

[07:53] Sophie: Thanks everyone, I'll follow up with the materials.

[07:57] (meeting ends)
